column1: I would die to recover an ancient relic of my faith that was lost long ago.
I will someday get revenge on the corrupt temple hierarchy who branded me a heretic.
I owe my life to the priest who took me in when my parents died.
Everything I do is for the common people.
I will do anything to protect the temple where I served.
I seek to preserve a sacred text that my enemies consider heretical and seek to destroy.
My mount is an extension of myself- we move as one.
Once I take an animal under my wing, it can count on me to protect it forever.
My pet mouse, [bonds.pet-mouse], travels in my pocket and keeps me company on my journeys.
I still own my grandfather’s bit which he used on the first warhorse he ever rode into battle.
I only remove the mink socks I made from my first successful trapping attempt to wash them.
All I have left of my childhood home after it burned is a scrap of fur from my favorite bearskin blanket.
My signet ring, a gift from the teacher who instructed me and one of their first finds.
I am restless in cities and towns; I feel connected to being in the field.
Knowledge is the only company I need.
My tools, without them I couldn’t work.
A fellow antiquarian with whom I share a close connection.
The first artifact I ever found, it started me down this journey.
My friend died from treachery in the arena and I’ll not rest until I’ve settled the score.
My former master is an ignoble coward, but his discipline made me what I am.
My blade is my life. I’ll fall if I lose it or break it.
My family sold me into slavery, and for that they will pay.
I love the crowd. Their cheers sustain my soul.
I owe a sum of money to a wealthy noble, and I cannot rest until she’s been paid back.
I have kept my service weapon in pristine condition, it remains an extension of myself.
My horse is my closest companion.
I remain in contact with other former soldiers from my cohort, they are like family to me.
A piece of wood carved into a symbol of my home.
My superior officer from my time in service, they offer sage advice.
My family, whom I miss dearly.
I can’t start my day without a mug of warm tea and honey.
I would never kill a bee! They produce food and medicine.
I can’t concentrate unless I’m chewing on some bee’s wax.
My father carved me a tiny wooden bee which I’ve never given away.
My creativity has helped me generate some unusual solutions to tricky situations.
I have to spend at least a few minutes of every day outside in nature or I get cranky.
My fellow cultists.
My hatred towards the gods is the only bond I need.
The signet ring I use to identify myself with my cult.
My mentor who inducted me into the cult.
A tome of dark knowledge given to me by my mentor.
The roiling void.
My trainer who entered me into competitions.
My family, who I hope to impress.
My fellow athletes who make it all worthwhile.
I feel a strong connection with the weak, remembering how I once was.
I have a lover back home whom I miss dearly.
The gymnasium where I train.
I have a certain patron whose embrace I miss dearly.
The first brothel I worked; it has always felt like home to me.
Coin is the only company I need.
The world is a dark place, I don’t feel strong connections with anyone.
A fellow concubine I met in my youth; we have always been there to support one another.
In a world like this, I can only rely on myself.
My family needs me to provide for them. They mean everything to me, which means I’ll do whatever it takes.
My kin have served this holding and its lords and ladies for generations. I serve them faithfully to make my lineage proud.
I can’t read the inscriptions on this odd ring, but it’s all I have left of my family and our history of loyal service.
I’m with the best friends a person can ask for, so why do I feel so lonesome and homesick?
I’ve found a profession where my skills are put to good use, and I won’t let anyone bring me down.
I found peace in a special garden filled with beautiful life, but I only have this flower to remind me. Someday I’ll remember where to find that garden.
My father taught me how to wield a sword, and how to locate water from miles away.
An opposing tribe slaughtered members of my tribe—including the person I loved—and I shall kill them for it.
A Grand Vizier from a faraway city owes me a large favor. It might be time to collect.
A warrior from a competing tribe showed me an unnecessary kindness once and we have become friends.
When the leader of a group of villains asked for my help, I led him into a trap. Now his people want me dead.
A warlord from far away seeks to destroy my tribe. I must find a way to destroy him.
I am the last living member of my tribe, and I cannot let their deaths go unavenged.
I follow the spiritual path of my tribe; it will bring me to the best afterlife when the time comes.
My best friend has been sold into slavery to devils, and I need to rescue them before it is too late.
A nature spirit saved my life when I was dying of thirst in the desert.
My takoba sword is my most prized possession; for over two centuries, it’s been handed down from generation to generation.
I have sworn revenge on the sheikh who unjustly banished me from the tribe.
The true gift of my destiny is the friendships I make along the way to it.
The benefits of completing this destiny will strengthen my family for years to come.
Trying to alter my decision regarding my destiny is an unthinkable affront to me.
How I reach my destiny is just as important as how I accomplish my destiny.
People expect me to complete this task. I don’t know how I feel about succeeding or failing, but I’m committed to it.
Without this role fulfilled, the people of my home region will suffer, and that’s not acceptable.
I want to engineer a treaty with far-reaching effects in the world.
I am carrying out someone else’s agenda and making favorable arrangements for my benefactor.
A deal I brokered went sour, and I am trying to make amends for my mistake.
My nation treats everyone equitably, and I’d like to bring that enlightenment to other nations.
A traveling orator taught me the power of words, and I want to emulate that person.
I fear a worldwide conflict is imminent, and I want to do all I can to stop it.
Something precious has been stolen from me, and I intend to take it back.
Someone very important to me died because of my mistake. It is never going to happen again.
I would do anything to show that I am not just a nobody.
In a dream I saw a great evil, and I could destroy it or bend it to my will.
I write down my life in a diary. If I lose it, no one will ever know who I was.
I am obsessed with the events of a particular day, and my mother’s face.
The desert, I could not live without it.
The breeze, which carries you through the dunes.
My family, who I stalked the desert with.
My favorite horse (or camel) with whom I share a strong connection.
There is a special person who I hope to see again.
Myself, it’s safer alone.
My connection to nature keeps me grounded.
I am a healer. I will always come to the aid of a fallen comrade.
My acupuncture needles were gifted to me by my favorite mentor.
My first anatomy book, though tattered and worn, cost my parents a month’s wages. I keep it as a symbol of their faith in me.
I am the only one in my family to receive a formal education, and I am proud of the skills I developed with it.
My word is my bond. I never renege on a promise to provide healing to someone.
I have family who are still slaves. One day, I will free them.
I still cling to my old traditions, from a time before I was a slave.
I will own my own land someday. I’m constantly looking out for the perfect spot.
I carry a possession that symbolizes my freedom. I would die to retrieve it.
Someone helped me escape. One day, I will repay them.
I was stolen from my homeland, and I yearn to return.
Exile has made me aware of a great evil only I can destroy.
I deeply value the friends I still have.
The hovel I live in is the only thing of value I have.
I’ve realized this is a better life and I never want to return to civilization.
My crimes were committed for the sake of the common good.
I owe my life to the person helped me when I was first exiled.
My family is tied to this land.
I will do anything to protect my farm.
My farm was destroyed by raiders or monsters. I will avenge it.
I am saving up to buy an estate with extensive farmland.
My farm is deep in debt and must be saved from the creditors.
I know the secrets of a strong harvest. I just need the right plot of land to settle down on.
When I lose a trusted friend or companion, I plant a tree upon their grave.
The voice of the forest guides me, comforts me, and protects me.
The hermit who raised me and taught me the ways of the forest is the most important person in my life.
I have a wooden doll, a tiny wickerman, that I made as a child and carry with me at all times.
I know the ways of civilizations rise and fall. The forest and the Old Ways are eternal.
I am driven to protect the natural order from those that would disrupt it.
I will end the monsters who killed my family and pulled me back into the adventuring life.
A disaster made me retire once. Now I will stop it from happening to anyone else.
My old weapon has been my trusted companion for years. It’s my lucky charm.
My family doesn’t understand why I became an adventurer again, which is why I send them souvenirs, letters, or sketches of exciting encounters in my travels.
I was a famous adventurer once. This time, I will be even more famous, or die trying.
Someone is impersonating me. I will hunt them down and restore my reputation.
Anti-slavery pirates rescued me from a slave ship. I owe them my life.
I still feel a deep attachment to my ship. Some nights I dream her figurehead is talking to me.
I was the ship’s captain until the crew mutinied and threw me overboard to feed the sharks. I swam to a small island and survived. Vengeance will be mine!

Years ago, when my city was attacked, I fled the city on a small fleet bound for a neighboring city. I arrived back in the ruined city a few weeks ago on the same ship and can remember nothing of the voyage.
I fell asleep when I was supposed to be on watch, allowing our ship to be taken by surprise. I still have nightmares about my shipmates who died in the fighting.
One of my shipmates was captured and sold into slavery. I need to rescue them.
I understand animals better than people, and the way of the hunter just makes sense.
I take great pride in providing my services to the wealthy and influential.
Natural spaces need to be tended and preserved, and I take joy in doing it when I can.
I need to ensure people know how to manage nature rather than live in ignorance.
Laws are important to prevent nature’s overexploitation.
I can be alone in the wilderness and not feel lonely.
I pursue wealth and power to win the love and respect of a distant paramour.
My secret loyalty to and belief in the power of my temple, sect, or faith is unshakeable; it alone shields me from (or gives me influence over) the powers of death and undeath.
As society scorned me, so I scorn it. I am dedicated to myself and myself alone.
I escaped a life of poverty by robbing a rich man’s grave. Shame and guilt still drive me to random acts of charity and atonement.
My (newfound?) friends are my bond; I am sometimes loyal to a fault, as they say.
My tools are symbolic of my unpleasant past; I carry them to always remind me that things can always get worse.
I can be happy living anywhere there is fertile soil.
I concentrate best when I’m chewing on teaberry leaves.
I treasure a perfectly preserved pressed rose from my first love.
I always have a trowel on me for digging up edible roots along the road.
Something about the feel of the sun’s warmth on my face and the sound of raindrops makes me giddy.
I would never part with my silver harvesting sickle. It was blessed by the druids of my home village.
The forest itself.
My mentor who inducted me into the ways of grove tending.
A particular forest spirit with whom I am close.
My family that I rarely get to see.
My duty to the forest.
A particularly large tree that I have watched over for many years.
I am on the run from a former master who seeks to destroy me.
I always looked up to the heroes and style my actions after my favorite one.
I am greatly indebted to a family member who never lost faith in me.
My otherworldly patron keeps tempting me to go back to my old ways. I do everything I can to silence them.
I left my bad life behind to try and impress someone I am infatuated with.
My terrible actions caused the death of someone close to me.
I am dedicated to my warlord. I may not be by his side, but I act in his interest.
I am not so close to any human being as I am to my horse, and this is how it should be.
I ran afoul of a dirty barbarian from another land. One of us will end up dead by the other’s hand.
During my time with the clan, I killed a villager with a family. I must atone for my offense.
I had a spouse, but she was murdered by another clan’s riders. I will see them dead by my hand before I die.
I owe a favor to the local lord’s heir, and I will see it paid before moving on.
I serve only those I pledge my loyalty to, and that is not an easy thing to earn.
I feel closer to the animals I hunt and derive sustenance from than I am to other people.
I ran afoul of an honorless mercenary from another land. Our paths will cross again, and one of us will not walk away.
During a raid on another clan, I accidentally killed a brave young man who was protecting his family. I have taken them on as my responsibility.
I could move on and earn more gold, but there are downtrodden here I must protect.
I am here to avenge the death of a clan mate.
I come from a long line of accomplished hunters. I want to make them proud.
There is a particular individual, large and succulent, that I have been trying to take down for several seasons.
Hunting is more than my subsistence, it is my job.
I always honor the gods of the hunt.
I dream of being the most famous huntress of all.
I keep trophies of my greatest kills.
I have kept my service weapon in pristine condition, it remains an extension of myself.
My horse is my closest companion.
I remain in contact with other former soldiers from my unit, they are like family to me.
The Imperial Seal I still carry, forever marking me as a member of the Empire.
My superior officer from my time in service, they offer sage advice.
My family, whom I miss dearly.
I started my career in a tavern, and I’ll end it running one of my very own.
I try to ensure stories of my companions will live on forever.
You want to take the measure of a person? Have a meal or drink with them.
I’ve seen the dregs of life pass through my door, and I will never end up like them.
A mysterious foe burned down my inn, and I will have my revenge.
One day, I want my story to be sung in all the taverns of my home city.
I’ve seen the future and I will stop at nothing to prevent it.
Each of my creations are sacred to me and I abhor anyone who would destroy them.
I’ve always craved the comfort of a family, but no one seems to understand me.
A mentor showed me I could be more than I was. I’ll never forget their lessons and want to help others in the same way.
Animals are my only true companions. At least the ones I don’t experiment on.
Who needs to win friends when you can simply make them from raw components?
I have a family to feed and protect. It has been some time since I saw them.
My brothers-in-arms are closer to me than any other. I would die for them.
I was trained by a master swordsman that went missing a few years ago.
A close friend gave me a dying wish with their last breath. I’ve been working to finish it for some time now.
A secret affair with a noble has me on the run. One day I will return to them.
My god abandoned me in a crucial moment, and I need to know why.
My parent’s legacy is a tissue of lies. I will never stop until I uncover the truth.
I am the only one who can uphold the family name.
My companions are my life, and I would do anything to protect them.
I will never forget the betrayal leading to my parent’s murder, but I will avenge them.
My honor and reputation are all that matter in life.
I betrayed my family to protect my friend who was a soldier in another free company.
My first mentor was murdered, and I seek the skills to avenge that crime.
I will become the greatest mercenary warrior ever.
I value the lessons from my teachers and trust them implicitly.
My family has sacrificed much to get me this far. I must repay their faith in me.
I will face any danger to win the respect of my companions.
I have hidden a map to an amazing and powerful magical treasure until I grow strong enough to follow it.
I’m making a game but need to know more about these creature’s habits to make the rules more realistic.
I can’t stand to see my research subjects suffer, even if it is the way of nature.
My family is constantly fretting over my safety, but I tend to forget they exist while researching.
My hometown is in danger and only I realize these monsters are to blame.
I am well respected within my field but am under a lot of pressure to keep publishing interesting data.
My party is the only thing keeping me alive. I do whatever I can to make sure they’re happy and healthy.
I want to experience every single aspect of the world.
I rely on my companions to teach me how to behave appropriately in their society.
I have a “sibling,” a child of my adopted parent that was raised alongside me, and now that sibling has been kidnapped!
My monstrous family deserves a place in this world, too.
I’m hiding from my monstrous family. They want me back!
An old enemy of my adopted parents is on my trail.
I have dreams where I see a loved one’s face, but I can’t remember their name or who they are.
I wear a wedding ring, so I must have been married before I lost my memories.
My mentor raised me; they told me that I lost my memories in a terrible accident that killed my family.
I have an enemy who wants to kill me, but I don’t know what I did to earn their hatred.
I know there’s an important memory attached to the scar I bear on my body.
I can never repay the debt I owe to the person who cared for me after I lost my memories.
I will do anything for those who supported me while I recovered from my ordeal.
I will never let the monsters who hurt those I love harm anyone else.
I help those who can’t survive without help.
I would die for those who went through the most horrific time of my life with me.
The only way to prevent anyone else from stumbling on the horrific disaster I encountered is to destroy all evidence of the ordeal.
Wholesome, natural life despoiled or transformed by evil forces must be cured or contained.
I have the support of my peers from the skaldic school I attended, and they have mine.
I will find and answer the Unanswerable Riddle and gain infamy.
I will craft an epic of such renown it will be recited the world over.
All my companions were slain in an ambush laid by cowardly trolls.
The cold waves call to me even across great distances. I must never stray too far from the ocean’s embrace.
It is inevitable that people fail me. Mead, on the other hand, never fails to slake my thirst.
One or more secret organizations are trying to stop me, which means I must be close to the truth.
My studies come before anything else.
No theory, however unbelievable, is worth abandoning without investigation.
I must uncover the truth behind a particular mystery, one my father died to protect.
I travel with my companions because I have reason to believe they are crucial to the future.
I once had a partner in my occult searches who vanished. I am determined to find them.
My clan was ambushed by slavers and it took me years to escape. I will bring them down if it’s the last thing I do in this life.
A wealthy merchant owes me a favor after I saved him from bandits.
After my parents were slain in battle, I was raised by one of their clan-mates.
A nobleman drove my clan from our ancestral grounds. I will make him pay.
There is an old woman who showed me great kindness after I was injured in battle, and I would travel any lengths if she asked.
The one who trained me to fight betrayed the clan. I must track them down and bring them to justice.
My instrument is an extension of myself.
The sounds of nature inspire every chord.
My teacher taught me all I know; I owe them everything.
I intend to play in the grand palaces of every nation.
The gods, who protected me during an ambush.
I had a patron at a previous court whom I grew quite attached to.
I will return to my home city someday and have revenge upon the elitist perfume consortium and corrupt shipping magnates who drove my dreams to ruin.
I have been experimenting and searching my whole career for the ultimate aromatic aphrodisiac. The “alchemists’ stone” of perfumery.
My home is safely far behind me now. With it go the unfounded accusations, spiteful rumors, and perhaps some potential links to a string of corporate assassinations.
I am cataloging an encyclopedia of flora and their various chemical, magical, and alchemical properties and applications. It is my life’s work.
I am dedicated to my craft, always seeking to expand my knowledge and hone my skills in the science and business of aromatics.
I have a loved one who is threatened (held hostage?) by an organized gang of vicious halfling thugs who control many of the “rackets” in the perfumeries in my home city.
A loyal servant with whom I cannot do without.
My wealth, symbol of my power.
My family, to whom I owe everything.
I feel a strong sympathy for urchins and street children, realizing I could have been born as one.
There is a member of another patrician family that I have strong feelings for.
A signet ring that reminds me of my past, and future.
My traveling companions keep me safe, and I must return the favor.
I was separated from someone important to me, and I long to see that person again.
I once found paradise, and part of me is still there.
It is my duty to make sure that others may travel as freely as I do.
I am haunted by something I once saw on a plane far away.
I love that which is strange and different.
I was a parent in my previous life. I miss my children so badly.
I latched onto the first person I met. They died shortly after and I must find a way to fix that.
I love being here. I can finally be the person I always wanted to be.
I am searching for the perfect wife, a quest I take more seriously than any other.
I am searching for the perfect husband, a quest I take more seriously than any other.
I have a family here, but I don’t remember any of them. I have a great fear of returning to them.
My religion does not exist here. Have I been abandoned by my god or sent here as a test?
My troupe, without whom I would be nothing.
The theatre where we performed back home.
The cheering crowds, inspired by our stories.
The script of my favorite play, that inspired me to write.
I only truly feel whole when I have a pen in my hand and parchment on the table.
My family, who supported my early efforts.
My physical fitness is my bread and butter.
I’m proud of my endurance, bigger men collapse under the loads I carry.
You can’t underestimate the value of good footwear. I always invest in sturdy boots.
My backpack is my lifesaver- there’s always something in it to help me out of a jam.
I cherish a rock I collected from the top of the highest mountain on my continent which I climbed carrying 96 pounds of gear on my back.
I always form a plan before undertaking a job. Without one, valuable resources are wasted.
I believe my mentor is greater than I will ever be, and I strive every day to impress them.
My fans are my true family.
I consider my work to be like a child to me. I am closer to it than anyone else.
I practice harder every day to impress an unrequited love.
My muse is an extra-planar being that is not always good to me.
I feel empty inside and just want someone to help fill that void. Anyone will do…
The school where I studied holds a special place in my heart.
I seek a patron or client who is worthy of my great skills.
The community of fellow professionals has made me the person I am today.
I pursued this career to obtain social status and respect.
One day I will prove that I am the greatest of all time at my profession.
Jealous rivals or malicious interlopers have destroyed my livelihood. Now it is time for revenge.
Our raider leader is evil in the purest sense of the word. I’ll deal with him in time.
Not long ago, I brought in a bandit for the city in which I now reside. I’m pretty sure he’ll want revenge sooner or later.
I ran afoul of a noblewoman and made off with some of her jewelry. I need to fence this stuff before someone recognizes the stolen pieces and reports me to her.
I confided the details of my past to the person I love. Now I can no longer find her/him.
Some of my brothers and sisters are still out there, but they are good at heart and should be saved.
There was a farmer who helped me get into the city. I will forever be in debt to his kindness.
I have a soulmate who has danced the Wheel of Rebirth with me many times, and I must now find them in this life.
I struggled against an old enemy in previous lives and this is my opportunity to settle things once and for all.
I made a terrible mistake in a previous life, and this reawakening is my opportunity to put things right.
My awareness is guiding me towards an enlightenment beyond the Wheel of Rebirth. I must minimize my attachment to this world.
My descendants from a previous life need my aid in this one.
My lives have been bound to a particular cause that I must take up again in this life, be it a nation, philosophy, or community.
My family is royalty and I loathe them, even if I miss them sometimes.
My partner was taken away from me by a corrupt regime. I will avenge them.
I can’t stand to see my beloved home fall into such a lowly place and want to restore it to glory.
Not enough people care about the children. We must fight for their future.
Art is the best way you can express yourself; the more disruptive the better.
My faith has kept you going this long, now if it could keep me going just a little longer…
I will one day return to the homeland that I was forced to flee, and there I will triumph.
I owe my life to someone who helped me and my family, a debt that I will never forget.
I will never forget where I came from, and I work to preserve my people’s culture and identity in our new home.
Things need to change if I and my people are to truly be at home here and I will lead that change.
We were betrayed when we were forced to leave our home, and I will never forget, or forgive.
I was forced to leave someone or something precious behind and still hold on to hope of an eventual reunion.
My daimyo is my lord and master, and I do all things to protect and honor him.

I listened to a murderer explain why he had killed his neighbor. He explained that the slain man had dishonored his daughter. When I spoke to others and confirmed this, I set him free. He now believes that he owes me a life debt.
I made a powerful enemy in the daimyo of a faraway land. He is likely to send assassins to try and kill me.
I came calling to collect a debt to my daimyo but was attacked by the debtor, who then fled. I will track down this traitor and bring him to justice.
I met one of my party members when they saved my life by making me aware of an ambush waiting for me.
I owe a personal debt to the person who forged my katana, for it sharpens easily and has never broken.
My elder sibling taught me how to find a safe hiding place in the city. This saved my life at least once.
I stole money from someone who couldn’t afford to lose it and now they’re destitute. One day I’ll make it up to them.
The street kids in my town are my true family.
My mother gave me an old brass lamp. I polish it every night before going to sleep.
When I was young, I was too scared to leap from the tallest tower in my hometown onto the hay cart beneath. I’ll try again someday.
A city guardsman let me go when they should have arrested me for stealing. I am forever in their debt.
My raid group was defeated and I was taken prisoner by a corrupt noble. I escaped.
The local shipwright has given me a lot of work and I owe him a debt of honor.
My son was kidnapped from me as a baby and I will find him.
I left my people when my father was killed at the hands of his political rival.
I took command of a vessel and crashed it on the rocks. I now owe that merchant a replacement.
The local noble has earned my respect and I will fight against his enemies.
My crew who are like family to me.
Illyria, which represents freedom from the Empire.
My ship, my true home.
I have someone back at port that I would give it all up for.
I would never betray my captain.
I do what I do for my family in need.
I blackmailed the wrong person, and now they’re after my head.
I fell into this trade by accident, after I killed a secret­broker and assumed their identity.
I carry a ledger of my most prized information with me at all times.
I often have my friends unknowingly carry out illegal tasks for me. This always/never makes me feel guilty.
The family business is in secret trading.
More than anything, I want to find the right person, settle down, and get out of this life.
I work with a partner that I’ve known for years. We rely on one another’s particular talents.
Though my training is long complete, the High Priest of my temple remains my personal mentor.
I remain in touch with many of the families to whom I provided my services.
The local nomarch has called on me to perform the Rites of the Dead on certain nobility in the past.
A foreign scholar has taken keen interest in Egyptian culture and sees my work as a point of study.
I sometimes visit the tomb of a relative to provide customary offerings.
My charge is paramount; if you can’t protect your charge, you’ve failed.
I was once saved by one of my fellow guards. Now I always come to my companions’ aid, no matter what the threat.
My oath is unbreakable; I’d rather die first.
There is no pride equal to the accomplishment of a successful mission.
I stand as a bulwark against those who would damage or destroy society, and society is worth protecting.
I know that as long as I stand with my companions, things can be made right.
I will perish before allowing others to suffer at the hands of Shadow.
I would have fallen into Shadow forever were it not for someone who helped me when I needed it.
I did something terrible that I truly regret and will spend the rest of my life trying to redress.
The creature of Shadow that scarred me is still out there, and I will destroy it.
I am haunted by someone I lost, either in memory, or literally by their ghost, who appears only to me.
I have few close friends but treasure them beyond measure.
I owe my life to my old slave master.
I am indebted to the one who freed me.
I will go to any lengths for revenge.
I will go to the ends of the earth to free others from slavery.
I fell in love with another slave who I will do anything to rescue.
I’ll tell any lie to hide my past.
My word is my bond; I have never welched on a deal, dishonored a handshake, or double-crossed a partner.
I am hastening to pay off an old debt, which could have assassins put on my trail any day now.
A corrupt magistrate ruined my good name and drove me underground; soon I will have my revenge.
Ill-gotten or not, a goodly portion of my gains goes to the humble, little monastery and the brothers there, who took me in that terrifying night so long ago.
I am known to have been a witness to a horrible crime. I became a smuggler as a means to survive while remaining in hiding from the crime’s perpetrator.
I will do whatever I must to prove my superiority and to discredit or destroy a past associate, who has turned into fierce rival.
I would do anything for my fellow soldiers. All they need to do is ask me a favor and I will be there for them.
One of the elders of my city took me under his wing and taught me the importance of thinking for myself while performing my duties. It is a lesson I will never forget.
I often fear that I have left behind a wake of children I know nothing about.
When in conquered lands, I like to walk among the people and speak with them, so they know that we are not there to harm them. Many would leap to my defense if asked.
My very first commander turned traitor, killed a few of his subordinates, and fled. I hope I meet him again so I can show him the “chain of command.”
I wander this world in search of higher meaning. Some think I have lost my mind, but I know there is more to life than blood and steel.
My calligraphy set; I never feel complete if I cannot write at the end of a long day.
The Academy; it’s home and where I feel I belong.
There’s a special someone back at the Academy that I can’t wait to see again.
I feel a great disconnect from those around me. I do not know what I seek.
I had a family. I need to find out what happened to my descendants.
Something has gone wrong with the flow of time, and I must redress this problem.
The city I came from has fallen from great heights. I can restore its prominence.
I must raise my fame and fortune to prove that I belong in this time.
I protect ancient sites from those who would seek to plunder their riches.
Someone else was also sent through time when I was. I need to find that person.
My books have helped me learn so many different languages.
I’ve marked every place I’ve ever visited on this travel-worn map.
I pride myself on my perfect accent for each language that I speak.
I’m so thankful for my hearing. Without it, I’d be cut off from the world.
What would I do without my companions? I’d be so lonely with no one to talk to.
I’ll never forget my first instructor. He opened my mind to the possibility that I could make a difference in the world… and I am!
The unwashed masses who flock to my words.
My teacher who taught me the proper way to spin words.
The sound of my own voice.
The orphans of the city hold a special place in my heart.
A certain someone who loves my voice almost as much as I do.
A scroll of poems which I draw hope from.
I like hunting because I like feeling big and powerful.
I hunt because my parents think I’m a worthless runt. I need to make them proud.
I was mauled by a beast on my first hunting trip. I’ve spent my life searching for that monster.
The first time I drew blood, something awoke within me. Every hunt is a search for the original ecstasy of blood.
My hunting companions used to laugh at me behind my back. They aren’t laughing anymore.
A close friend funded my first hunting expedition. I am forever in their debt.
I killed a friend to prove my loyalty to my warlord. I *don’t* regret it.
I was forced into slavery, but clawed my way to freedom. I still have family out there.
My subordinates look to me for guidance, and I must provide it. They are the closest I have to family.
I hate the warlord I serve, and would love nothing more than to see them deposed.
If I serve my leader well, I will ride beside them to the afterlife.
I have a rival, and I will do anything to undermine them.
A nobleman owes me a favor for fishing him out of shark infested waters.
A small child I rescued relies upon me for survival.
I’m in love with someone, and they claim to return my love, but they will not follow me away from the clan.
I’m sworn to avenge the death of my father at the hands of a warring tribe’s rabid dog of a leader.
I must return to my clan one day and report all I have found in the outside world.
I don’t know why this rogue keeps following me around, but they’ve helped me too many times to turn his back on him when they’re in trouble.
A walking stick I have had with me since home.
I have someone in a town I once visited I hope to visit again.
I was stuck once; I never will be again.
I have a soft spot for the forgotten of society.
My home town is a good place and I would do anything to protect it.
A small animal I found in my travels is now my constant companion.
